fulfillment_judgment.auxiliary_material: The study details the biological context of inosine generation via adenosine deaminase (ADA) expressed by engineered probiotics in hypoxic tumor regions. It reports immune outcomes associated with inosine accumulation, such as increased CD8+ T cell infiltration and M1 macrophage polarization in mouse colorectal cancer models. The text notes that inosine can serve as an alternative carbon source for T cells under glucose-depleted conditions and describes the use of lamivudine as an internal standard for quantification.
fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Search for peer-reviewed methodological papers or consensus guidelines specifically validating LC-MS/MS or GC-MS protocols for inosine and SCFA quantification in human clinical samples (serum, plasma, tumor biopsy). Look for studies that establish reference concentration ranges for these metabolites in cancer patients versus healthy controls. Investigate whether any oncology or metabolomics societies have published standard operating procedures for these specific analytes.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The supplied material does not provide standardized protocols for human serum or tumor tissue, as all experiments were conducted in mouse models (MC38 subcutaneous and orthotopic CRC). There is no information on short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) quantification methods or parameters. The study does not offer cancer-specific reference ranges for human patients or healthy controls, nor does it cite consensus statements or guidelines for clinical metabolite quantification. The analytical method described is specific to this research context rather than a validated clinical standard.
fulfillment_judgment.useful_material: This study provides specific LC-MS/MS analytical parameters for quantifying adenosine and inosine in murine tumor tissues, including column type (ZORBAX RRHD Eclipse Plus C18), mobile phase gradients (water/acetonitrile with 0.1% FA), flow rate (300 µL min⁻¹), and MRM transitions (inosine 269.1/136.8, adenosine 268.1/135.9). It also describes a solid-phase microextraction (SPME) technique for measuring free metabolite concentrations in the tumor microenvironment using HLB-PAN fibers and kinetic calibration. A baseline adenosine concentration of 0.04 µM is reported for control mouse tumors.
